question_text: Was Japan's education ministry (MEXT) procurement system hacked?
answer_text: Yes, by the ministry's own account. MEXT says a third party got unauthorised access to servers of its government procurement system, found on Oct 1, 2026. Up to 1,778 email addresses and 163,953 company records may have leaked.
label: Confirmed

question_text: What data may have leaked from the MEXT procurement system?
answer_text: Email addresses (up to 1,778) and companies' names, their representatives' names and other details (up to 163,953 records) stored in the system's database. The ministry says these are the figures it can confirm so far.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Who was behind the MEXT procurement system intrusion?
what_would_settle_it: The ministry, the police or another official body naming the attacker or saying how the intruder got in.

question_text: Has the leaked MEXT data been misused?
answer_text: The ministry says it has found no sign so far that the data was made public or misused. It is still investigating.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Is the MEXT procurement system still working?
what_would_settle_it: A ministry notice, or reporting with its own sourcing, saying whether the procurement system is in use, stopped or restored. The ministry says only that the system's communications in and out were cut off.
